chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no divorce except what is intended by it as divorce, and there is no Zihar except what is intended by it as Zihar.

key_terms.ظِهَار: Zihar (a form of divorce where the husband likens his wife to his mother)

ai.seo_question: What is the role of intention in the validity of divorce and Zihar in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores that verbal declarations of divorce (Talaq) and Zihar are contingent upon specific intention (niyyah), distinguishing them from mere casual speech. This principle ensures legal precision, preventing accidental utterances from triggering binding marital consequences, a view supported by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid who emphasize the internal intent behind the external words.
